Tell me in about 200 words why people in India are switching to UPI, with a short list of 3 reasons
6:57 PM

People in India are switching to UPI because it makes paying faster, cheaper and easier than cash, cards or bank transfers. It began as a way to send money to friends and is now how many people pay for chai, groceries, rent and bills.

Three main reasons:

It is quick and simple. Scan a code or pick a contact, enter the amount and approve with your PIN. The money reaches the other person in seconds, at any hour, even on holidays.
It is almost free. Most payments between people and at shops carry no charge for the user. Small sellers like it too, since they need no card machine, just a printed code.
It works across banks and apps. One app can link several bank accounts, and any UPI app can pay any other. A street vendor and a big store accept the same kind of payment, so you rarely need a backup option.

Cheaper phones and data helped, and the habit spread fast once family, friends and shops all used it. Every payment also shows up in your app, which makes tracking your spending easier than counting notes.

Plan a 3 day trip to Jaipur for my parents
7:00 PM

Here is an easy-paced 3 day Jaipur plan for your parents, with mornings for sightseeing and rests in the afternoon. November is a good time to go, with mild days.

Day 1, the old city: City Palace and Jantar Mantar in the morning, then a view of Hawa Mahal from the street. In the evening, a slow stroll through Johari Bazaar for jewellery and block prints.
Day 2, forts: Amber Fort early to beat the crowds, with a jeep up so they skip the steep climb. Stop for photos at Jal Mahal on the way back. Rest after lunch, then dinner with a folk show at Chokhi Dhani.
Day 3, gentle wrap-up: Albert Hall Museum and Birla Mandir in the morning, then a Rajasthani thali lunch. Leave time for last-minute shopping at Bapu Bazaar before they head home.

Staying near MI Road or the old city keeps each day's travel short. Where are they travelling from? I can then look at train and stay options.
